images.caption: Figure 1:Overview.Top:SABER evaluates attribute–object binding by reassigning fixed sets of objects and attributes.Bottom:Synthetic text-only finetuning improves binding in text and image representations, boosting unimodal and cross-modal retrieval on SABER and existing benchmarks

Figure 2:SABER multiple-choice questions.Each query has four candidates with 2–10 attribute–object pairs: one preserves the bindings, while the others form hard negatives by reassigning attributes. For two-object examples, one negative instead replaces an object or attribute. Although only images are shown, the accompanying captions enable evaluation within and across modalities.

Figure 3:Nested SABER chains.Nine linked MCQs form a chain from two to ten objects, read left to right and top to bottom. Each successive query adds one binding while preserving all earlier ones. Half of SABER’s MCQs are organized into such chains, allowing later correct candidates to serve as additional positives for earlier queries in large-gallery retrieval.
